question.text: Under the derivatives framework described in the NISM workbook, an exchange that fulfils the L.C. Gupta Committee criteria and wishes to start trading in a derivative segment (equity, currency, or IR) must apply to which regulator for grant of recognition under SCRA?

answer.text: SEBI - the exchange applies to SEBI for grant of recognition under SCRA to start trading in the derivative segment, with this applying across equity, currency and IR derivative segments
RBI grants exchange recognition for the currency and IR derivative segments, while SEBI grants it for the equity derivative segment
Recognition under SCRA is no longer required for derivative segments; only a SEBI no-objection certificate is needed
The exchange applies to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs under the Companies Act for derivative-segment recognition

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook p.177 (NISM Series-VIII, December 2025) states that an exchange fulfilling the L.C. Gupta criteria applies to SEBI for grant of recognition under SCRA Section 4 to start trading in derivatives. This framework is applied across the derivative segments (equity, currency, IR). The keyed option states only this directly source-supported application path. The Trap: RBI co-regulates the underlying currency/IR markets but does not grant exchange recognition; SCRA recognition has not been replaced by a "no-objection" route; the Ministry of Corporate Affairs governs companies generally, not exchange recognition. The audit flagged the original because p.179 separately notes that recognition under SCRA "can be granted by the Central Government", which made the blanket "SEBI grants recognition" wording inconsistent with the SCRA text unless the delegation to SEBI was made explicit. Note: The original was ambiguous because pp.177 and 179 of NISM Series-VIII (December 2025) phrase the recognising authority differently (SEBI on p.177 vs Central Government on p.179). The stem has been reframed to ask who the exchange applies to under the workbook's derivatives framework (p.177), making SEBI uniquely correct without depending on the SCRA delegation wording.
